core_obligations: Reduce to showing that the fifth condition implies the first (proof lines 6671).

For an arbitrary weak ideal of definition, note that proving the statement for the intersection with the chosen ideal implies it for the original one, so that one may assume the arbitrary ideal is contained in the chosen one (proof lines 6671-6679).
Use that a power of the chosen ideal lies in the arbitrary one, so that the quotient of the two ideals is nilpotent (proof lines 6677-6679).

Write down the diagram of quotients with exact rows, observe that the smaller kernel is the extension of the nilpotent quotient of ideals, and conclude by the criterion for finiteness of type through a nilpotent ideal (proof lines 6679-6692).
proof_roadmap: Reduction to the implication from the fifth condition (proof lines 6671).
Comparison of the two ideals (proof lines 6671-6679).
The diagram of quotients with its exact rows (proof lines 6679-6689).
Conclusion by the nilpotent criterion (proof lines 6689-6692).
difficulty_reason: In the situation of the preceding lemma on quotients of restricted power series algebras, the lemma adds that when the source ring is admissible -- for instance adic -- the four equivalent conditions there are also equivalent to a fifth one, in which finiteness of type of the induced map of quotients is required for a single ideal of definition rather than for all of them or for a cofinal system (statement lines 6660-6669). The proof shows that the fifth condition implies the first: for an arbitrary weak ideal of definition one has to show that the corresponding map of quotients is of finite type, and since the statement for the intersection of that ideal with the chosen one implies the statement for the ideal, one may assume the arbitrary ideal is contained in the chosen one (proof lines 6671-6679). Because the chosen ideal is an ideal of definition, a power of it lies in the arbitrary one, which makes the quotient of the two ideals nilpotent, and the two kernels appearing in the evident diagram of quotients are then related as required: the small kernel is the extension of the nilpotent quotient of ideals, and the map of quotients is obtained from a finite type map by passing to a quotient by a nilpotent ideal (proof lines 6679-6692). The claim is H2: the reduction to a comparable ideal, the construction of the commutative diagram with exact rows, and the application of the nilpotent case of the finite type criterion are each displayed.
